data.title: We Ran A Stock Scan For Earnings Growth And LC Spólka Akcyjna (WSE:APL) Passed With Ease
data.description:
Investors are often guided by the idea of discovering 'the next big thing', even if that means buying 'story stocks' without any revenue, let alone profit. But as Peter Lynch said in One Up On Wall Street, 'Long shots almost never pay off.' Loss making companies can act like a sponge for capital - so investors should be cautious that they're not throwing good money after bad.

If this kind of company isn't your style, you like companies that generate revenue, and even earn profits, then you may well be interested in LC Spólka Akcyjna (WSE:APL). Now this is not to say that the company presents the best investment opportunity around, but profitability is a key component to success in business.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

LC Spólka Akcyjna's Earnings Per Share Are Growing

Generally, companies experiencing growth in earnings per share (EPS) should see similar trends in share price. That means EPS growth is considered a real positive by most successful long-term investors. Shareholders will be happy to know that LC Spólka Akcyjna's EPS has grown 33% each year, compound, over three years. As a general rule, we'd say that if a company can keep up that sort of growth, shareholders will be beaming.

Top-line growth is a great indicator that growth is sustainable, and combined with a high earnings before interest and taxation (EBIT) margin, it's a great way for a company to maintain a competitive advantage in the market. The music to the ears of LC Spólka Akcyjna shareholders is that EBIT margins have grown from 4.8% to 12% in the last 12 months and revenues are on an upwards trend as well. That's great to see, on both counts.

You can take a look at the company's revenue and earnings growth trend, in the chart below. To see the actual numbers, click on the chart.

See our latest analysis for LC Spólka Akcyjna

LC Spólka Akcyjna isn't a huge company, given its market capitalisation of zł3.7m. That makes it extra important to check on its balance sheet strength.

Are LC Spólka Akcyjna Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

Seeing insiders owning a large portion of the shares on issue is often a good sign. Their incentives will be aligned with the investors and there's less of a probability in a sudden sell-off that would impact the share price. So as you can imagine, the fact that LC Spólka Akcyjna insiders own a significant number of shares certainly is appealing. Owning 41% of the company, insiders have plenty riding on the performance of the the share price. This should be a welcoming sign for investors because it suggests that the people making the decisions are also impacted by their choices. Of course, LC Spólka Akcyjna is a very small company, with a market cap of only zł3.7m. So despite a large proportional holding, insiders only have zł1.5m worth of stock. That might not be a huge sum but it should be enough to keep insiders motivated!

Should You Add LC Spólka Akcyjna To Your Watchlist?

For growth investors, LC Spólka Akcyjna's raw rate of earnings growth is a beacon in the night. This EPS growth rate is something the company should be proud of, and so it's no surprise that insiders are holding on to a considerable chunk of shares. On the balance of its merits, solid EPS growth and company insiders who are aligned with the shareholders would indicate a business that is worthy of further research. It is worth noting though that we have found 3 warning signs for LC Spólka Akcyjna (1 doesn't sit too well with us!) that you need to take into consideration.

There's always the possibility of doing well buying stocks that are not growing earnings and do not have insiders buying shares. But for those who consider these important metrics, we encourage you to check out companies that do have those features. data.title: Just Three Days Till mySafety Group AB (STO:SAFETY B) Will Be Trading Ex-Dividend
data.description:
Readers hoping to buy mySafety Group AB (STO:SAFETY B) for its dividend will need to make their move shortly, as the stock is about to trade ex-dividend. The ex-dividend date is usually set to be two business days before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. It is important to be aware of the ex-dividend date because any trade on the stock needs to have been settled on or before the record date. Thus, you can purchase mySafety Group's shares before the 7th of October in order to receive the dividend, which the company will pay on the 13th of October.

The company's upcoming dividend is kr00.45 a share, following on from the last 12 months, when the company distributed a total of kr1.35 per share to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that mySafety Group has a trailing yield of 7.4% on the current share price of kr018.20. We love seeing companies pay a dividend, but it's also important to be sure that laying the golden eggs isn't going to kill our golden goose! So we need to check whether the dividend payments are covered, and if earnings are growing.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Dividends are usually paid out of company profits, so if a company pays out more than it earned then its dividend is usually at greater risk of being cut. mySafety Group paid out 103% of its earnings, which is more than we're comfortable with, unless there are mitigating circumstances.

Generally, the higher a company's payout ratio, the more the dividend is at risk of being reduced.

View our latest analysis for mySafety Group

Click here to see how much of its profit mySafety Group paid out over the last 12 months.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Stocks in companies that generate sustainable earnings growth often make the best dividend prospects, as it is easier to lift the dividend when earnings are rising. If earnings decline and the company is forced to cut its dividend, investors could watch the value of their investment go up in smoke. It's encouraging to see mySafety Group has grown its earnings rapidly, up 38% a year for the past five years.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. mySafety Group has delivered an average of 5.8% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past nine years of dividend payments. It's good to see both earnings and the dividend have improved - although the former has been rising much quicker than the latter, possibly due to the company reinvesting more of its profits in growth.

Final Takeaway

Has mySafety Group got what it takes to maintain its dividend payments? We're not enthused to see mySafety Group's dividend was not well covered by earnings over the last year, although it is great to see earnings growing. We're unconvinced on the company's merits, and think there might be better opportunities out there.

If you're not too concerned about mySafety Group's ability to pay dividends, you should still be mindful of some of the other risks that this business faces. For example, mySafety Group has 3 warning signs (and 1 which shouldn't be ignored) we think you should know about.

data.title: Teradyne Stock In Focus After New Memory And MicroLED Test Platform Launches
data.description:
• Teradyne recently launched the Magnum E2 high speed memory tester and the Iris 100 microLED optical test platform, both aimed at complex AI data center and advanced display workloads.
  • These platforms extend Teradyne's test coverage into high speed DRAM, NAND and microLED arrays, which could influence product mix, R&D payback and long term demand visibility.
  • We will look at how Teradyne's investment narrative is shaped by Magnum E2's focus on AI driven high speed memory testing.

Scan beyond Teradyne and line up other potential AI hardware beneficiaries by reviewing our curated 90 AI infrastructure stocks while this buildout of compute and memory capacity is front of mind.

Teradyne Investment Narrative Recap

To own Teradyne, you need to believe its heavy exposure to AI centric test demand can offset swings in product mix, memory pricing pressure and the higher cost of rolling out new platforms like Magnum E2 and Iris 100. The near term swing factor is whether AI related capital spending actually flows into Semi Test and memory orders at the pace management has been pointing to.

The biggest current risk is clear. If AI data center and advanced packaging CapEx pauses or slips, order intake across Semi Test, Product Test and Robotics could soften just as Teradyne is leaning into higher R&D and go to market spending. That would make the guided gross margin pressure more painful.

The Magnum E2 launch matters most right now. It squarely targets high speed DRAM and NAND test tied to AI data centers, an area management has already framed as a major opportunity with memory revenue above US$200m for three straight quarters and a 2026 memory TAM that is expected to be materially larger than 2025.

If Magnum E2 is adopted into qualification and high volume manufacturing flows, it can support that memory test narrative and help Teradyne lean against product mix pressure. The execution watchpoint for investors is whether this platform, alongside compute and robotics spend, converts into stable gross margins and enough volume to justify the higher operating expense base.

What The Current Teradyne Forecasts Assume

Analysts sketch a Teradyne path that leans heavily on AI centric testing and robotics, then attach some fairly specific numbers to that story. The forecast pencils in revenue growth of 22.7% a year over the next three years, which is a brisk pace for an automated test equipment specialist already tied closely to large data center and memory customers.

On earnings, the consensus view points to profit of US$1.2b today rising to US$2.6b by 2029, with margins moving from 25.8% to 31.4% over the same period. That implies earnings a little more than doubling, even before considering the small projected decline in share count of 0.17% a year, although there is a wide spread between the most bullish and most cautious analyst estimates. For you as an investor, the key question is how comfortable you are anchoring on a 2029 earnings figure when so much of the current demand is tied to AI buildouts and advanced memory cycles that can ebb and flow.

Those profit and margin paths also feed directly into how the Teradyne stock is valued. Analysts are working with a future P/E of 37x on the 2029 earnings estimate, down from 54.5x today and below the current 46.9x multiple for the wider US semiconductor group. That lower assumed multiple matters because it shows the current story is not just about higher earnings; it also leans on the market being willing to pay less for each dollar of projected profit than it does right now.

The revenue side of the equation carries its own hurdle. To line up with the consensus price target, the model expects Teradyne to reach US$8.2b of sales by 2029 alongside the US$2.6b earnings figure. That top line track effectively ties the company to sustained AI related capital spending, higher test intensity in advanced packaging and continued traction in robotics, all of which could influence how Magnum E2 and Iris 100 adoption translates into order flow and product mix.

Teradyne's narrative projects US$8.2b revenue and US$2.6b earnings by 2029. This assumes 22.7% yearly revenue growth and earnings rising a little more than 2x from US$1.2b today.

Exploring Other Perspectives

You also have a much more cautious Teradyne story on the table. The more pessimistic analysts worry that AI orders bunch up, then cool, which could strain Magnum E2 payback. They were only penciling in roughly US$6.8b revenue and US$1.9b earnings by 2029 before this news. That gap shows how widely opinions can differ, so explore multiple viewpoints before you commit capital.

The Pathways CCS news does not change the key short term catalyst, which is execution on production efficiency and disciplined capital spending. It does, however, sharpen the biggest risk already on the table, that high emission oil sands exposure could face rising carbon costs and tighter regulation that pressure unit economics.

The bullish view pointed to a Fair Value of £0.94, a price implied by expectations that government hydrogen spending and ITM’s TRIDENT and NEPTUNE platforms would support 54.6% revenue growth and a 5.8% profit margin assumption.

The bearish camp saw Fair Value closer to £0.40, based on concerns that tighter financing, policy reversals and geopolitical risks would pressure contract decisions, even if revenue rose 54.1% with the same margin assumption and a 57.7x future P/E.

What The Results Changed For The ITM Power Thesis

The clearest new fact was ITM Power’s half year move from £15.534 million of revenue and a £28.86 million loss in H1 2025 to £18.026 million of revenue and a £14.16 million loss in H1 2026, with net margin improving from a loss of 185.8% to a loss of 78.6%. That mix of higher sales and smaller losses supported the optimistic case, but profitability assumptions stayed unproven.

The lesson is simple. When a story hinges on future margin repair, keep checking whether losses are shrinking faster than revenue is rising and whether that gap closes in reported net margin, not just in commentary.

What ITM Power’s Run Up Might Already Be Pricing In

ITM Power now trades at £1.02, and this Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that level. This flags a concern that the recent 59.6% move from the start of the year may already bake in generous expectations.

The key question is what must keep going right for today’s price to make sense. This includes the assumption that ITM Power converts its backlog into profitable projects despite financing, policy and competition pressures.

data.title: If EPS Growth Is Important To You, V2 Retail (NSE:V2RETAIL) Presents An Opportunity
data.description:
It's common for many investors, especially those who are inexperienced, to buy shares in companies with a good story even if these companies are loss-making. But as Peter Lynch said in One Up On Wall Street, 'Long shots almost never pay off.' Loss making companies can act like a sponge for capital - so investors should be cautious that they're not throwing good money after bad.

In contrast to all that, many investors prefer to focus on companies like V2 Retail (NSE:V2RETAIL), which has not only revenues, but also profits. Even if this company is fairly valued by the market, investors would agree that generating consistent profits will continue to provide V2 Retail with the means to add long-term value to shareholders.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

How Fast Is V2 Retail Growing Its Earnings Per Share?

In the last three years V2 Retail's earnings per share took off; so much so that it's a bit disingenuous to use these figures to try and deduce long term estimates. As a result, we'll zoom in on growth over the last year, instead. Impressively, V2 Retail's EPS catapulted from ₹2.32 to ₹4.92, over the last year. It's not often a company can achieve year-on-year growth of 112%. That could be a sign that the business has reached a true inflection point.

It's often helpful to take a look at earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margins, as well as revenue growth, to get another take on the quality of the company's growth. EBIT margins for V2 Retail remained fairly unchanged over the last year, however the company should be pleased to report its revenue growth for the period of 63% to ₹34b. That's a real positive.

In the chart below, you can see how the company has grown earnings and revenue, over time. Click on the chart to see the exact numbers.

See our latest analysis for V2 Retail

While it's always good to see growing profits, you should always remember that a weak balance sheet could come back to bite. So check V2 Retail's balance sheet strength, before getting too excited.

Are V2 Retail Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

It's pleasing to see company leaders with putting their money on the line, so to speak, because it increases alignment of incentives between the people running the business, and its true owners. So it is good to see that V2 Retail insiders have a significant amount of capital invested in the stock. Notably, they have an enviable stake in the company, worth ₹11b. This totals to 15% of shares in the company. Enough to lead management's decision making process down a path that brings the most benefit to shareholders. Looking very optimistic for investors.

While it's always good to see some strong conviction in the company from insiders through heavy investment, it's also important for shareholders to ask if management compensation policies are reasonable. Our quick analysis into CEO remuneration would seem to indicate they are. For companies with market capitalisations between ₹38b and ₹154b, like V2 Retail, the median CEO pay is around ₹39m.

V2 Retail's CEO took home a total compensation package of ₹6.0m in the year prior to March 2026. That looks like a modest pay packet, and may hint at a certain respect for the interests of shareholders. CEO remuneration levels are not the most important metric for investors, but when the pay is modest, that does support enhanced alignment between the CEO and the ordinary shareholders. Generally, arguments can be made that reasonable pay levels attest to good decision-making.

Should You Add V2 Retail To Your Watchlist?

V2 Retail's earnings have taken off in quite an impressive fashion. The sweetener is that insiders have a mountain of stock, and the CEO remuneration is quite reasonable. The sharp increase in earnings could signal good business momentum. Big growth can make big winners, so the writing on the wall tells us that V2 Retail is worth considering carefully. We don't want to rain on the parade too much, but we did also find 1 warning sign for V2 Retail that you need to be mindful of.

There's always the possibility of doing well buying stocks that are not growing earnings and do not have insiders buying shares. But for those who consider these important metrics, we encourage you to check out companies that do have those features.
